Updated assessment incorporating SLOOS insights:
- Credit supply: The April 2020 Senior Loan Officer Opinion Survey shows broad-based tightening of standards and terms across C&I (including middle-market firms) and CRE (nonfarm nonresidential, multifamily, construction/land development), with wider loan-rate spreads, higher credit line costs, tighter LTVs, and banks focusing on existing clients. Banks cited COVID-19, a deteriorating economic outlook, reduced risk tolerance, liquidity needs, supervisory/accounting considerations, and industry-specific problems.
- Credit demand: Weaker demand in CRE and construction/land development; HELOC demand largely unchanged but with tighter standards. Notable exception: stronger demand and some relative easing/unchanged standards for government-backed mortgages.
- Implications vs FOMC statement: While the Fed highlights improved financial conditions and strong policy backstops (LSAPs, repo, and credit facilities), SLOOS indicates the bank-lending channel remains restrictive, reinforcing downside risks to activity and employment. This points to a more negative near-term macro/financial backdrop than suggested by market-functioning improvements alone.

Net: Dovish policy stance with meaningful backstops, but SLOOS-confirmed tightening in bank credit amplifies headwinds. Adjusting more negative from the prior read.
